HandaProject 001

project 001

Handa

AI legal aid for overseas Filipino workers

A mobile app that walks a migrant worker through a guided intake in their own language, maps their situation to the right legal remedy in their home country, stores contracts and pay records in a secure vault, and routes the case to a partner pro-bono organization.

Built solo end to end: product definition, partner ecosystem, information architecture, and code. The design constraint that shaped everything — an app used by people under employer surveillance cannot leak. Data minimization and on-device storage came before features.

Storefront AgentProject 002

Project
002 / 006

project 002

Autonomous
Storefront Agent

Unattended publish pipeline with a pre-publish gate

A design goes in one end; a published, screened listing comes out the other. A folder watcher picks up a new design, Claude Vision reads it and picks the products it suits, the agent generates SEO-optimized copy, waits on mockup rendering, and publishes to the storefront. Every run is logged to SQLite; results arrive by Telegram. A companion dashboard scores demand signals week over week and feeds the results back into what the agent is permitted to make.

The part I’d point a governance team to is the pre-publish gate: nothing ships without clearing trademark screening, duplicate detection, and a demand check against live market data, then routing to PASS / REVIEW / BLOCK. It is a working instance of the thing policy documents usually only describe — a human-reviewable checkpoint between an autonomous model and an irreversible action.

WPS Incident RecordProject 003

Project
003 / 006

project 003

WPS Incident Record

Coercion at sea, coded against the law it breaks

A structured evidentiary database that codes Chinese coercive activity in the West Philippine Sea against the specific UNCLOS provisions and 2016 arbitral award findings it implicates — turning a decade of dispersed incident reporting into a record built to withstand legal scrutiny.

It ingests Philippine Coast Guard and AFP incident reports, National Maritime Council statements, diplomatic protests, released imagery, and live AIS from aisstream.io and Global Fishing Watch, then produces structured case records. Extraction is model-assisted and every record passes human adjudication before entering the database, with sourcing and chain of custody documented to the Berkeley Protocol on Digital Open Source Investigations.

project 004

AI Fluency OS

The curriculum I built to close my own technical gap

A deployed web app that structures sixty days of AI study across four parallel tracks — concepts, technical, theory, policy — and enforces one fixed daily ritual: twenty minutes learning a concept, twenty building something, twenty reading a primary source. Progress persists server-side and syncs across devices.

I built it because the available options were either too shallow to survive a technical meeting or too deep to finish. The policy track — EU AI Act, NIST, frontier safety frameworks — is rebuilt on technical footing rather than treated as separate literacy.

project 005

Ma Biche

French immersion chosen by mood, not by level

A daily French listening and reading companion — podcasts, music, radio, literature — curated by mood rather than sorted into difficulty tiers. A new selection every day, so deciding what to listen to never becomes the reason not to.

Built to keep a third language alive without a course structure. One editorial judgment, executed cleanly: maintaining fluency is a habit problem, not a content problem.

SolBoundProject 006

Project
006 / 006

project 006

SolBound

A recovery companion where progress is the user’s own to keep

A sobriety and recovery app built around a private journal and a milestone journey, with on-chain proof-of-attendance as an optional layer rather than a requirement. Local-first storage by default: the sensitive record stays on the device, and nothing about a user’s recovery is legible to anyone who didn’t earn it.

Five illustrated companions mark the stretches of the road — one per chapter — alongside a daily mood check, an anonymous forum, and a reading library. The companion evolves with meetings logged, so the record of the work is the reward for it.

selectedwriting

Policy analysis, memos and research written across graduate work, government and a current working paper. Summaries only.

001

The Canary in the Dragnet

How the Philippines–Gulf labour corridor normalises digital control. Argues that migrant populations are not simply surveilled more heavily than citizens but are the proving ground where AI surveillance infrastructure is piloted, legitimised and de-risked before it diffuses into general-population governance — legal exceptionalism and debt-bonded entry making them the lowest-resistance environment for unproven tooling. Sits deliberately outside the border-tech literature’s focus on the Global North asylum axis, and offers a falsifiable test: trace each tool from corridor deployment to citizen-facing use.

Research dossier
In progress
2026
002

Proposed Enhancements to the Monitoring Framework for FFD4

A monitoring framework for commitments made at the Fourth International Conference on Financing for Development, covering all seven action areas: domestic public resources, private business and finance, development cooperation, trade, debt sustainability, international financial architecture, and science, technology and capacity building. Sets short-term indicators against the Addis Ababa Action Agenda baseline, names the measurement gaps in each area, and recommends longer-term monitoring architecture.

Capstone · team
For UN DESA
2025
003

Facial Recognition Technology in the Criminal Justice System

A memo to the Office of the Mayor of Metro Manila setting four conditions before any city-wide deployment of facial recognition: stakeholder consultation across every level of government first, disclosure to residents about how their data will be used and where groups may opt out, representative training data with accountable and transparent vendors under continuous evaluation, and human oversight of every output — partnership with the model rather than dependence on it.

Policy memo
2024
004

Applying the Juntos Approach to Brazil’s Federal Agencies

Written in the voice of a chief advisor to the president of Brazil. Argues for scaling the participatory-governance practices the Juntos programme proved in medium and small cities up to the federal agencies: an annual best-practice conference between agencies, civil-society survey evidence verified against government databases so funds follow the priorities constituents actually name, and financed public participation platforms — weighed against the risk of over-reliance on new technology and misread data.

Policy memo
2024
005

Immigration Reform and the Bipartisan Coalition

Written in the voice of a political advisor to a US senator in the closing years of the Bush administration. A positioning strategy that breaks with the administration’s approach and builds an immigration bill on two arguments at once — the labour-market contribution of immigrants and the case for stronger geographic and economic security — using the split inside the Republican party to assemble cross-party support, and costing the strategy honestly against the Democratic support it would strain.

Policy memo
2024
006

The Kafala System and Migrant Worker Protection in the Gulf

Reviews the reform record across the GCC states — Kuwait’s minimum wage for domestic workers alongside its stricter nationalisation rules, Oman’s forced-labour law that excludes domestic workers, Qatar under World Cup scrutiny, Saudi Arabia’s thirty-eight labour amendments — against the sponsorship system that survives all of it. Sets out why the ILO’s standard-setting runs into a structural wall when a state’s independent labour-law mechanism is tied to its own economic interest.

Working paper
Draft
007

An Analysis of Sotheby’s Corporate Social Responsibility

Assesses the firm’s CSR against its own stated commitments on access for excluded communities, environmental responsibility, and lending its platform to raise funds. Finds the benefit-auction model plays to a real strength but is close to unassessable for beneficiary impact, that a house whose clout rests on exclusivity makes an awkward platform for inclusive representation, and that little in the firm’s practice evidences the environmental language in its own Code of Conduct.

Analysis
2023
